representative.title: Protocol for the growth and maintenance of mammalian cell lines
representative.assay: routine mammalian cell growth and maintenance
representative.operation: maintenance and passaging of standard mammalian cell lines
representative.specimen: HeLa cells; adaptable to standard mammalian cell lines
representative.platform: adherent cell culture flask, incubator, and biosafety cabinet
representative.selectionNote: Selected for its recent, general mammalian maintenance scope, stable DOI, named authors and affiliations, public abstract, and explicit CC-BY basis for publicly published user protocols. Cell-line-specific medium, coating, and incubator adaptations remain necessary.

screened.title: Basic Cell Culture Maintenance: Splitting Cells v1
screened.reason: Directly relevant to routine splitting, but narrower in operation and older than the selected general maintenance record.

screened.title: Passaging and colony expansion of human pluripotent stem cells by enzyme-free dissociation in chemically defined culture conditions
screened.reason: Specific to human pluripotent stem cells and defined enzyme-free conditions, so it should not stand in for broad mammalian routine maintenance.

screened.title: Mouse Embryonic Stem Cell Maintenance for Differentiation
screened.reason: A useful stem-cell maintenance record, but its mouse embryonic stem-cell scope is narrower than the assigned general mammalian category.

coverageGaps: Routine maintenance spans adherent, suspension, primary, and stem-cell variants; these were not merged into one universal record.
The selected record is HeLa-oriented and does not provide a universal medium, coating, or incubator specification for every mammalian line.
nextSearchSuggestions: Search separately for suspension-cell maintenance protocols.
Search primary mammalian cell maintenance by tissue and coating requirement.
Search for cell-line-specific medium and confluency records when a line is selected.

representative.title: CELL STORAGE-01-Freezing and Thawing Protocol for Adherent Cell Lines
representative.operation: thawing and recovery of adherent mammalian cell lines
representative.specimen: adherent cell lines including MCF7, HUVEC, A549, and synovial fibroblasts
representative.platform: water-bath thawing, culture flask, optical microscopy, and confluence recovery QC
representative.methodVariant: adherent-cell thawing with rapid cryoprotectant removal
representative.selectionNote: Selected because the public record is explicitly focused on thawing and post-thaw quality for adherent cell lines, names the validated cell-line scope, provides authors, affiliation, DOI, date, and public status, and has an explicit CC-BY basis under the site terms.

screened.title: CELL STORAGE-02-Freezing and Thawing Protocol for Suspension Cell Lines v1
screened.reason: Directly relevant but specific to suspension cell lines, whereas the selected representative covers adherent lines.

screened.title: PBMC Thawing Protocol v1
screened.reason: Primary immune-cell recovery is a meaningful variant, but it is not a general adherent mammalian cell-line thawing record.

screened.title: Improving Cell Recovery: Freezing and Thawing Optimization of Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells
screened.reason: Open-access recovery optimization provides useful corroboration, but the experimental system is induced pluripotent stem cells rather than routine adherent cell lines.

coverageGaps: The selected record is for adherent human-derived lines; suspension, primary-cell, and pluripotent-stem-cell recovery remain separate variants.
No single universal thawing record was identified that covers all mammalian cell types and recovery media.
nextSearchSuggestions: Search suspension-cell thawing and recovery as a separate child category.
Search primary-cell and PBMC recovery protocols separately.
Search stem-cell thawing protocols with post-thaw survival or attachment readouts.

representative.title: Freezing/Cell Banking
representative.operation: cryopreservation and long-term banking of dural cells
representative.selectionNote: Selected because the public record explicitly identifies banking into cryovials for long-term liquid-nitrogen storage and exposes a stable DOI, author, affiliation, date, public status, and CC-BY site-term evidence. The workflow is dural-cell specific, so generalization across cell lines is recorded as a gap.

screened.title: Cryopreservation and banking of mammalian cell lines
screened.reason: Canonical general cell-line banking protocol, but the publisher landing page was challenge-gated during this run and record-level reuse licensing was not verified.

screened.title: Mammalian Cell Culture: Freezing v1
screened.reason: Relevant general freezing record, but its title and available metadata do not establish a banking workflow as clearly as the selected record.

screened.title: Rate-controlled Cryopreservation and Thawing of Mammalian Cells
screened.reason: Strong controlled-cooling mammalian-cell variant, but it combines freezing and thawing and has less explicit cell-bank scope.

coverageGaps: The selected banking record is dural-cell specific; master/working bank release criteria and cell-line-independent validation were not established.
Cryoprotectant, cooling-rate, and post-thaw QC choices may differ substantially for suspension, primary, and stem-cell systems.
nextSearchSuggestions: Search master-cell-bank and working-cell-bank release criteria separately.
Search suspension and primary-cell cryopreservation by cell type.
Compare controlled-rate cooling with passive freezing for the intended cell line.

representative.title: Cell Culture Mycoplasma Detection by PCR
representative.operation: PCR screening of cell-culture samples with gel-electrophoresis readout
representative.platform: conventional PCR and agarose gel electrophoresis
representative.methodVariant: consensus-sequence PCR for broad mycoplasma detection
representative.selectionNote: Selected for its direct cell-culture mycoplasma PCR focus, peer-reviewed label, public DOI/author/date metadata, and explicit page-level copyright statement. The page states that Bio-protocol LLC is the exclusive licensee; no reuse permission is assumed from public access, and full procedure text requires login.

screened.title: Detection of Mycoplasma in cell cultures
screened.reason: Canonical protocol-level alternative, but the publisher landing page was challenge-gated during this run and record-level license evidence was not verified.

screened.title: Testing for mycoplasma in cell culture by PCR
screened.reason: A newer PCR-focused alternative, retained for follow-up comparison because its public metadata was less complete in this run.

screened.title: Detecting Mycoplasma Contamination in Cell Cultures by Polymerase Chain Reaction
screened.reason: Relevant book-chapter protocol record, but the full publisher content and record-level reuse terms were not publicly verified.

coverageGaps: The representative is a PCR workflow; luminescence, enzymatic, staining, and culture-based tests remain separate assay variants.
The public page exposes metadata and an abstract/materials view, but the full procedure text is login-gated.
nextSearchSuggestions: Search luminescence and enzymatic mycoplasma detection as separate variants.
Search direct institutional QC SOPs with record-level licenses.
Verify primer coverage and analytical sensitivity against a current validation source before implementation.

selfCheckNotes: Category IDs are exactly the assigned four IDs and remain in packet order.
Every representative has a stable HTTP(S) source URL, source record ID, and DOI or an explicit null.
License evidence URLs were recorded from explicit source or platform statements; no reuse permission was inferred from access alone.
Only metadata, citations, source URLs, license evidence, and short evidence notes were stored; protocol steps and long passages were omitted.
The output was written, re-read, parsed as JSON, and checked against the packet contract.

runNotes: Protocols.io public records were selected for the first three categories because the page status, DOI metadata, and platform terms were directly verifiable.
The mycoplasma representative is a public Bio-protocol record with explicit copyright/licensing language but login-gated full text; this limitation is preserved in the record and coverage gaps.
